newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lorraine says would welcome DHL Rhine hub.
newsitem.headline: Lorraine says would welcome DHL Rhine hub.

text.p: France's north-east Lorraine region said on Friday it would welcome DHL Worldwide Express's Rhine Valley cargo hub project, following the collapse of a plan to install the hub at Strasbourg in neighbouring Alsace.
Lorraine today published full page advertisements in the national French press saying "Lorraine welcomes DHL" and offering to locate the hub at its Nancy-Metz airport.

On September 18, the day after the plan's collapse, DHL said it had received "a significant number" of telephone calls that morning from other French provincial airports offering their facilities as an alternative to Strasbourg.
Strong local opposition to proposed night flights was a key factor in the effective dropping of the Strasbourg project.
The Nancy-Metz airport, 110 kilometres to the north-west, was among the original candidates for the location of DHL's hub although the express operator finally decided on Strasbourg.

"We are not pushing for an early meeting with DHL to re-discuss the project because we recognise the need for a "cooling-off" period after what happened in Strasbourg," a Lorraine regional council spokesman told Reuters.

"What we are saying, through our campaign is that the company would be very welcome in Lorraine, should it re-consider Metz-Nancy-Lorraine airport as a potential site for its Rhine Valley hub," he added.

The Lorraine region is looking to re-negotiate on the basis of the offer made to DHL when its delegation visited the airport earlier this year - financing an extension to runway and aircraft aprons to accommodate wide-bodied aircraft as well participating towards the construction costs of hub facilities.

"All the necessary infrastructure required by DHL to operate from the airport could be in place within the space of three months, including buildings, as the land belongs to the public authority," the spokesman said.

"As well as its geographical position, it was the economic argument which persuaded DHL in favour of Strasbourg - the offer of existing facilities, operable immediately, in a part of the airport previously used for military activities," he added.

"However, its urban location meant it an environmental weakness which would not be the case with Nancy-Metz airport as this is situated in a rural area and also has excellent surface transport communications," he said

By the turn of the century, the Lorraine region will have improved motorway links and be served by the TGV Est high-speed passenger train network, which will also be able to provide freight transport, the spokesman added.
DHL's main shareholders are Deutsche Lufthansa AG and Japan Airlines Co Ltd who each hold a 25 percent stake. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+434 171 542 5017
